precepts.text: Such an high priest, holy, harmless, undefiled, who needeth not daily, as those high priests, to offer up sacrifice, first for his own sins, and then for the people's: for this he did once, when he offered up himself.
precepts.point: Aaron dipped his finger in the blood and put it upon the horns of the altar, burnt the fat and kidneys and caul, the guts, upon the altar, and the flesh and the hide he burnt with fire without the camp; you keep reading it over and over, without the camp.

note.label: Leviticus 9: The Glory of the Lord Appears

precepts.why:
The priest had to make an atonement for himself first, and then offer the offering of the people. Hebrews opens up that order: “such an high priest became us, who is holy, harmless, undefiled, separate from sinners, and made higher than the heavens; Who needeth not daily, as those high priests, to offer up sacrifice, first for his own sins, and then for the people’s: for this he did once, when he offered up himself.”

Aaron slew the calf of the sin offering, which was for himself, before the people’s. Christ, the high priest after the order of Melchisedec, is holy, harmless, and undefiled, and had no sins of his own to atone for; he offered up himself once.

precepts.text: There came a fire out from before the Lord that consumed the offering on the altar; that is the fire that devoured Nadab and Abihu.
precepts.point: The fire that went out from the Lord was the same fire that came out from before the Lord in Leviticus 9 and consumed the burnt offering upon the altar.

note.label: Leviticus 10: Strange Fire and the Charge of the Priesthood

precepts.why:
“And there went out fire from the Lord, and devoured them.” That is the same fire from the chapter before: “And there came a fire out from before the Lord, and consumed upon the altar the burnt offering and the fat: which when all the people saw, they shouted, and fell on their faces.”

The fire that came out from before the Lord and consumed the burnt offering upon the altar in Leviticus 9 is the fire that devoured Nadab and Abihu in Leviticus 10. The same fire accepted the offering that was done as commanded, and consumed the priests who offered strange fire “which he commanded them not.”

points: On the eighth day Moses called Aaron and his sons and the elders of Israel: a young calf for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering, without blemish; and for the people a kid of the goats for a sin offering, a calf and a lamb of the first year without blemish, a bullock and a ram for peace offerings, and a meat offering mingled with oil, the meat offering again being grain, not flesh.

note.label: Leviticus 9: The Glory of the Lord Appears

points: For today the LORD will appear unto you: they brought what Moses commanded before the tabernacle, and all the congregation drew near and stood before the LORD, the whole nation gathered in front of the tabernacle.

note.label: Leviticus 9: The Glory of the Lord Appears

points: Moses said unto Aaron, go unto the altar, and offer thy sin offering and thy burnt offering, and make an atonement for thyself, and for the people. The priest had to make an atonement for himself first, and then offer the offering of the people.

That is the order Hebrews opens up: the high priests of the law needed daily to offer up sacrifice first for their own sins and then for the people's; but Christ, the high priest after the order of Melchisedec, is holy, harmless, and undefiled, and offered up himself once.

note.label: Leviticus 9: The Glory of the Lord Appears

points: Aaron dipped his finger in the blood and put it upon the horns of the altar, burnt the fat and kidneys and caul, the guts, upon the altar, and the flesh and the hide he burnt with fire without the camp; you keep reading it over and over, without the camp.

note.label: Leviticus 9: The Glory of the Lord Appears

points: Aaron brought the people's offering: the goat of the sin offering was slain and offered for sin as the first, the burnt offering was offered according to the manner, and he took an handful of the meat offering, the grain, and burnt it upon the altar.

note.label: Leviticus 9: The Glory of the Lord Appears

points: He slew the bullock and the ram for a sacrifice of peace offerings for the people, the word read in Ephesians of Christ our peace, and the blood was sprinkled upon the altar round about, the blood the law keeps returning to.

note.label: Leviticus 9: The Glory of the Lord Appears

points: The breasts and the right shoulder Aaron waved for a wave offering before the LORD, a washed piece lifted and waved, as Moses commanded.

note.label: Leviticus 9: The Glory of the Lord Appears

points: Aaron lifted up his hand toward the people and blessed them, and came down from offering the sin offering, the burnt offering, and the peace offerings; and Moses and Aaron went into the tabernacle, and came out and blessed the people.

note.label: Leviticus 9: The Glory of the Lord Appears

points: The glory of the LORD appeared unto all the people, and there came a fire out from before the LORD and consumed upon the altar the burnt offering and the fat; which when all the people saw, they shouted, and fell on their faces. The whole nation standing before the tabernacle saw the Most High answer the offering with fire.
